title: Operational Priority Orchestrator for Reliability Commitments
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Goal: Build an operational orchestrator that continuously scores running initiatives against active reliability commitments (SLI targets + error budget runway) and recommends automatic priority adjustments, temporary rollout throttles, or escalation to SRE/PMs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Dashboard view that lists active initiatives with a computed "score" (SLI attainment, burn rate, rollout exposure). 2) Automated signals that can tag initiatives as: Maintain, Throttle, Escalate, or Deprioritize. 3) Two configurable policies: conservative (manual approval for actions) and permissive (auto-throttle on runway < 7 days). 4) Audit log entries for each automated action with links to the originating telemetry. 5) Integrations: Console rollouts UI, Alerts (PagerDuty), and Initiative tracker to surface changes.
proposed_design_summary: We will calculate a per-initiative risk score derived from: weighted SLI deviation (50%), error budget burn rate (30%), rollout scope/exposure (10%), and deployment velocity (10%). Scores map to orchestration actions. Scoring logic runs hourly and stores snapshots for the last 90 days. Actions are surfaced in the Reliability Console; permissive policy will trigger rollout throttles via the rollout API.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: - Tradeoff: aggressive auto-mitigation reduces incident blast radius but increases developer friction; we provide policy modes to minimize false positives. - Decision: use telemetry-derived rollout exposure instead of product-reported exposure to avoid manual tagging overhead. - Alternate: manual-only workflow rejected due to need for rapid response during thin error budget runway.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (MVP) - compute scores, surface dashboard, create manual action buttons (Q4). Phase 2 - policy engine with permissive/conservative profiles and automated throttle actions via rollout API (Q1). Phase 3 - audit + rollback orchestration and cross-team SLAs (Q1-Q2).
tasks: 1) Telemetry mapping and SLI adapter (ENG-80421). 2) Scoring service prototype (ENG-81002). 3) Dashboard UI + detail flyout (DES-902). 4) Policy engine and action runner (ENG-81234). 5) Rollout API hooks and permissions (ENG-82011). 6) E2E tests and chaos scenarios (SRE collaboration).
risks_and_mitigations: - Risk: false positives triggering throttles -> mitigation: start with permissive=false and only allow manual actions for first 4 weeks. - Risk: mismatched SLI definitions across teams -> mitigation: validation layer and opt-in for initiatives. - Risk: audit/legal concerns -> mitigation: retain full action logs, require PM approval for policy switch to permissive.
success_metrics: - Reduction in P1 incidents attributable to rollout changes by 25% in 90 days. - Mean time to detect & mitigate overload events reduced from 18m to <9m for initiatives covered. - 95% of automated actions include a human review within 72 hours. - Adoption: 40% of active initiatives opt in to permissive policy within first quarter post-launch.
